display_title: Netanyahu Sparks Debate over Shadow Economy
display_title_he: נתניהו מעורר סערה סביב תכנון כלכלת צללים
short_summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu raised eyebrows by disclosing preparations for a potential shadow economy if international sanctions hit Israeli banks. Economists warn that disconnecting Israel from global banking would severely damage its economy.

sources.name: Walla
sources.title: הכל בשביל הקמפיין: נתניהו בדרך לרסק את כלכלת ישראל

paragraphs: During a series of pre-election media appearances on Economic Channel 10, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sparked intense debate by raising the prospect that Israel might eventually need to transition toward a shadow economy. Interviewed by veteran journalist Roi Katz, the Prime Minister suggested that the nation should actively prepare for potential international financial sanctions targeting its banking system. To address this unprecedented possibility, Netanyahu disclosed that he had already instructed officials to establish a dedicated team to examine preparations for shadow-banking solutions. Such contingencies would likely involve expanding reliance on cryptocurrency infrastructure to bypass standard international banking channels if traditional financial routes were severely restricted.

The Prime Minister’s remarks also revisited previous discussions regarding the potential end of United States defense assistance, drawing direct comparisons to earlier controversial statements he made about adopting a "Spartan economy." Currently, Washington provides Israel with approximately $3.8 billion annually in military funding—a strategic bilateral partnership rooted in Israel’s long-standing role as a stable forward post in the Middle East. Political commentators immediately debated whether Netanyahu’s alarming statements were an inadvertent slip of the tongue or a calculated electoral strategy designed to instill fear among voters ahead of the upcoming election. Under the latter view, fostering anxiety about extreme economic isolation serves to convince the public to vote for a seasoned leader capable of managing existential threats, echoing long-standing political messaging promoted by his supporters.

Financial analysts and economic experts quickly detailed the catastrophic consequences of disconnecting Israel from global financial networks. Unlike self-contained or autocratic states operating under international embargoes, Israel’s high-tech and export-driven economy depends entirely on interconnected international infrastructure, specifically the SWIFT global payment network. Cutting off domestic banks from this system would paralyze standard import and export operations, terminate foreign credit lines, and prevent Israeli investors from repatriating capital earned from selling securities on foreign stock exchanges. Economists emphasize that total banking sanctions represent a "doomsday weapon" typically reserved for dictatorial regimes such as Iran, Russia, or North Korea.

The contentious interview forms part of a broader media blitz by Netanyahu across selected regional radio stations—such as Eliko’s Radio Lev HaMedina—and targeted digital outlets, even as he continues to avoid major commercial television stations like Channel 12 and Channel 13. During these appearances, he has reportedly reprimanded interviewers who depart from his preferred narrative. While critics dismiss his dark economic forecasts as unsubstantiated political rhetoric, industry observers warn that such high-level statements can cause immediate financial disruption. Analysts noted that public discussion of shadow banking by a sitting prime minister risks unsettling institutional investors and sparking volatility in bank shares on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange. Market participants hope that reassuring official statements will emerge before trading opens, mitigating potential panic while national debate over economic policy intensifies.

facts.fact: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu gave an interview on Economic Channel 10 to journalist Roi Katz ahead of upcoming elections.
Netanyahu discussed preparing for potential international banking sanctions by contemplating a transition to a shadow economy, including cryptocurrency systems.
Netanyahu confirmed he ordered the establishment of an official team to examine preparations for a shadow economy scenario.
Netanyahu revisited potential loss of US military assistance ($3.8 billion annually) and referenced earlier comments about a 'Spartan economy'.
Commentators debated whether the statements were a slip of the tongue or a deliberate pre-election campaign strategy to instill voter anxiety.
Disconnecting Israel from the SWIFT international banking system would block import/export transactions, foreign credit lines, and capital transfers from overseas stock exchanges.
International banking sanctions are typically reserved for totalitarian regimes such as Iran, North Korea, or Russia.
Netanyahu has been conducting a campaign blitz across radio stations (including Eliko's Radio Lev HaMedina) while avoiding television Channels 12 and 13.
Market commentators expressed concern that Netanyahu's statements could unsettle investors and impact bank stocks on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange when trading opens.
